model_annotation: This bar chart compares the "effect" values across nine linguistic families—IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic—for six different language models: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). The horizontal axis lists the linguistic families in order, while the vertical axis represents the "effect" on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each linguistic family has a grouped set of six bars, one for each model, with error bars indicating variability. The bars are arranged in the same order for each group, corresponding to the legend. In most linguistic families, the mBERT-R₂ (light green) and XLM-R₂ (dark green) models show higher effect values compared to the others, especially in IE-Indic, where mBERT-R₂ reaches approximately 20 and XLM-R₂ reaches about 18. The Semitic family shows high variability, particularly for XLM-B₂ (dark red), which reaches nearly 20 with a large error bar. In contrast, the Uralic and Isolate families show very low effect values across all models, often near 0. The IE-Indic family generally exhibits the highest effect values among all groups, while the Uralic and Isolate families consistently show the lowest. No bars are visually emphasized beyond the standard error bars and color coding.
